metadata.technology_specification: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) System
metadata.technology_reasoning: The triple quadrupole LC–MS/MS system is the industry-standard technology for targeted quantitative analysis in analytical chemistry and biochemistry due to its high sensitivity and selectivity. It is widely adopted in pharmaceutical, environmental, and food safety applications owing to its capability to perform tandem mass spectrometry with triple quadrupole mass analyzers coupled to liquid chromatography.

components.reasoning: Core subsystem for separating analytes in mixture prior to mass spectrometric detection, procured as a distinct, standardized module including pump, injector, column compartment, and autosampler.

components.component: Ion Source Module (e.g., Electrospray Ionization, ESI)
components.reasoning: Essential front-end interface that ionizes the liquid effluent from LC for MS analysis; Ion sources are modular and commonly procured separately, with ESI being the prevalent type in LC–MS.
Primary mass filter that selects precursor ions, a dedicated and distinct component fundamental to triple quadrupole operation.
Central collision/reaction cell where selected ions are fragmented by collision-induced dissociation, a discrete and critical ion optics component.
Second mass filter selecting product ions; essential component forming the tandem MS structure unique to triple quadrupole systems.
Detects and amplifies ion signals post mass analysis, a separate module vital for signal transduction and data output.
Vacuum pumps maintain high vacuum environment for mass analyzer operation; standard subsystem with dedicated supply chain.

components.component: Control and Data Acquisition Electronics (DAQ) Module
components.reasoning: Electronic subsystem managing instrument control, data collection, and communication, typically a distinct PCB-based system.
Structural framework housing all modules, providing mechanical support, EMI shielding, and operator interface mounting; standard as a separate assembly.
